analysis: The only change in docs/developer/test.md is a documentation edit. The 'Last updated' stamp moves to 2026-11-13 (line 3). Lines 2192-2197 add a description of run-isolation regression tests for CI runner routing: the request header, exact run-qualified Linux and Mac labels with and without sizes, and fallback for generic or other-run responses. The text says two successful route responses must produce incompatible label sets for different runs, and states that this models GitHub's all-label selection rule without claiming a live runner or VM test. No code, workflow, protocol, key handling, attestation, cache or authorization behavior changes in the supplied evidence. No threat-model asset or boundary changes: A-001, the A-015 to A-017 serving authorization assets, TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011 and T-041 are untouched. The surrounding unchanged text in the units describes fixtures, cluster checks and release tests, and was read as context only. I identified no security regression and no new attack surface. The added text is an accurate-sounding limitation statement and makes no live-security claim. Remaining integration question: the actual scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py and the routing step it exercises are outside this batch. I cannot verify that they implement the described run-isolation behavior. That is a doc/code accuracy question, not a finding.
